body: Oh great, caught between Shepherd and Wattsi. @sideshowbarker would a workaround here be using `data-dfn-type` directly?

> Oh great, caught between Shepherd and Wattsi. @sideshowbarker would a workaround here be using `data-dfn-type` directly?

Not sure if that will fix it but I guess that’s worth trying at least.

> Error: <dfn> element found with redundant dfn="" attribute; dfn is <dfn> element containing "DOM manipulation task source"; previous heading contents are "8.1.6.4 Generic task sources"
> Error: Element found with dfn type name and redundant export attribute; dfn is <dfn> element containing "DOM manipulation task source"; previous heading contents are "8.1.6.4 Generic task sources"


Otherwise, we can update Wattsi to drop the offending check(s). Is it both of those errors that are th problem, or is it only one of them (and the other is fixable)?
I guess @domenic should also check this since I guess we added some Wattsi infrastructure to avoid getting the weird indexing of HTML, but it seems like it still happens...
Alas, seems it still breaks.

Ah, yeah, it looks like the check is being done after the translation, so my strategy of working around the check by using the expanded forms doesn't work:

https://github.com/whatwg/wattsi/blob/0cc7791926b0fe44eeb0fd62e504ec7a81202386/src/wattsi.pas#L1192-L1196

It sucks because this is a good check in general, it's just the Shepherd heuristics that are throwing us off... I wish Shepherd wouldn't apply heuristics to HTML.

I guess we should add some sort of `data-bypass-shepherd-heuristics=""` and if Wattsi sees that, it should delete the attribute and not issue a warning?

> I guess we should add some sort of `data-bypass-shepherd-heuristics=""` and if Wattsi sees that, it should delete the attribute and not issue a warning?

Sounds good to me. I can write up a Wattsi patch for it today my time

> I wish Shepherd wouldn't apply heuristics to HTML.

You don't, at least not with the current state of HTML, as it would make a lot of definitions be detected incorrectly, and thus not be linkable without doing things wrong (or not at all, if they collide in a way that Bikeshed can't distinguish between). 

Unless y'all've done a lot of work to make the spec consistently obey the dfn contract since I last checked? If so, then sure, we can def turn off the heuristics.

> Unless y'all've done a lot of work to make the spec consistently obey the dfn contract since I last checked?

Yes, to my (limited) understanding of all this stuff at least, we have

> If so, then sure, we can def turn off the heuristics.

OK — so to be clear, if you do that, it’ll fix the problem our CI is reporting here? If so, then I will hold off on doing the proposed `data-bypass-shepherd-heuristics=""` patch for Wattsi
A bunch of work has been done already and #6361 does more of it. It's probably at the point where disabling Shepherd heuristics would be good so we can fix remaining breakage manually.
@tabatkins @plinss can the heuristics be disabled for the HTML Standard?

In principle, yes, but several of those were added explicitly *for* the HTML spec, and it's not clear how much of the anchor database would break. Some significant testing would have to be done before simply turning them all off. (And I also suspect a lot of other markup would need to the changed in the HTML spec to make up for what the heuristics are doing, tho that can probably be handled in your generator.)
@plinss what I'm saying is that we have made those changes to the HTML Standard markup. If you look at the source you'll see we export things now and use Bikeshed's attribute model for that.

Ok, cool. If you're doing that, then the heuristics shouldn't be coming in to play anyway. Explicit markup should always win. If you have examples where that isn't the case, I'd love to hear about them because that'd be a bug that needs fixing.

I'm confused about where you think the heuristics are getting in your way.

I'm also not really keen on the idea of adding a switch to turn them off. Aside from debugging generators I don't see a use case that won't cause breakage in other specs. A better approach might be to have the spec parser emit warnings when the heuristics apply, tho you'd have to then run a local instance against your output to get them as they just go into server logs in production, but you could add it to your CI toolchain.
@plinss this very thread is an example, no? "DOM manipulation task source" doesn't default to type `dfn`.
It feels like folks are looking for a broader fix, but for this particular issue, the heuristics could be updated so definitions with spaces are never considered interfaces.
Heh, we're running into this in https://github.com/fedidcg/FedCM/pull/378/files#r1047957373. It's not a big deal of course, but is there anything that this issue is stalled on?

> Heh, we're running into this in [fedidcg/FedCM#378 (files)](https://github.com/fedidcg/FedCM/pull/378/files#r1047957373). It's not a big deal of course, but is there anything that this issue is stalled on?

I know we have https://github.com/whatwg/wattsi/pull/149 ready to merge, and I _think_ that would resolve this too. But see the discussion there — we don’t have agreement that making a change to wattsi is the best fix; a reasonable argument continues to be made that the better fix would be:

- Shepherd should stop using heuristics
- In the absence of a `data-dfn-type` attribute, Bikeshed and Respec should default to typing `dfn` elements as type `dfn` — rather than requiring every element to have an explicit `data-dfn-type`

It looks like once https://github.com/tabatkins/bikeshed/issues/1761 is done Bikeshed will stop using Shepherd and probably won't suffer from these sorts of problems with its database, too. So that's my current best plan...

Will we still have the problem where Reffy exposes non-exported definitions to Bikeshed and Bikeshed then decides those are more relevant somehow than exported definitions? Or does Reffy not index those at all and potentially end up breaking explicit `spec=html` references?

cc @dontcallmedom

reffy/webref collect and publish all the definitions, not just the exported ones (among other things because we wanted to make it easier for bikeshed to adopt it, IIRC); but I agree bikeshed should favor exported definitions to private ones, and possibly only accept using private ones with a specific flag.

Thanks, I guess that's still something that needs fixing. But it also seems like we'll at least no longer have heuristics for HTML, which is a big win. Really appreciate all the work you put into that @dontcallmedom!
This appears to be fixed now that Bikeshed has switched to WebRef. I have successfully linked to the DOM manipulation task source using `[=DOM manipulation task source=]`.
I followed up with FedCM and Notifications.
